text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Peruvian commandos storm the hijacked Japanese ambassador's residence, killing rebels and freeing all hostages alive except one.
- The Central Narcotics Bureau arrests four suspected traffickers including a 15-year old girl in a one-room flat in Toa Payoh with 1.6 kg of heroin seized during the operation.
- The Urban Redevelopment Authority puts up tender for developing four well-located residential sites, including a prime condominium plot next to Tanglin Club.
- Singapore Airlines sells a Boeing 747-300 combi jet and is seeking buyers for two other Boeings.
- Foreign exchange market traders worry G7 meeting may prick the recent US dollar bubble.
- Malaysian Treasury Secretary-General Clifford Herbert says the government's did not tell institutional investors in the country to stabilise the Malaysian stock market.
- The Philippines imposes curbs on property loans.
- New drilling data and move by Suharto-linked group may brighten prospects that gold in Indonesia's Busang mine will revive as Nusamba Group increases its stake in the project.
- Straits Times Industriails Index plunges to a 27-month low despite Wall Street's surge.
- Saudi Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud joins Ong Beng Seng to expand 34 Planet Hollywood outlets in 23 countries.
- Business Times Survey shows Singapore Airlines, Hongkong Land and Singapore's big four banks among 10 most profitable companies listed in the local bourse.
- Bookshop Popular Holdings offer its shares at 36 cents each, two cents lower than the recent Raffles Medical Group offer and one cent more than Chuan Soon Huat's offer.
